Add Godot documentation to this file. The Godot version is 4.5

Documentation should be added in two places. Each line should begin with ## and include BBCode tags for formatting. Use [br] for line breaks.

First, add class-level documentation directly after the extends line. Include an empty comment line after the class name. The documentation should include:
- A brief description of the class
- A [b]Signals:[/b] section listing all signals with descriptions

Here is an example of correcly formatted class-level documentation
extends StlToMesh (Included for formatting purposes, do not copy this line)
## StlToMesh
##
## [i]Utility to convert an STL file into a Godot ArrayMesh and align it to the planning grid.[/i][br]
## [b]Signals:[/b][br]
## - [code]example_signal[/code]: Emitted when an example event occurs.[br]

Second, add function documentation above each func line. The documentation should include:
- A brief description of what the function does
- A [b]Parameters:[/b] section (only if the function has parameters, excluding parameters prefixed with underscore)
- A [b]Emits:[/b] section (only if the function emits signals)
- A [b]Returns:[/b] section (only if the function has a non-void return type)

Here is an example of correcly formatted function documentation
## Import a directory of STL files into a new DragonbiteTileSet[br]
## [b]Parameters:[/b][br]
## [code]path[/code] : [String] — filesystem path to the directory containing
## [code].stl[/code] files.[br]
## [code]set_name[/code] : [String] — unique name to assign to the imported tile set.[br]
## [b]Emits:[/b][br]
## - [code]import_started(total_tiles: [int])[/code] once at the start of an import[br]
## - [code]tile_imported()[/code] after each tile is imported[br]
## [b]Returns:[/b] [void][br]
